svg.aria-label: Diagram of flip's parser on pages do-be job-size divided-by s' page-size $'s ceil. The tokenizer splits on whitespace only, so s' and $'s stay whole words. Recursive descent walks one function per precedence level, from rbind down to primary, and builds a tree: do-be pages, then ACCESS ceil over divided-by, whose operands are job-size and s' page-size. Because $'s binds last, ceil applies to the whole quotient.
svg.text: flip — reading a line that is mostly words
Flibbity tokenizes on whitespace alone, then parses by recursive descent with one function per precedence level.
pages do-be job-size divided-by s' page-size $'s ceil
PARSER (each level calls the one below)
admit-job works out how many pages a job needs …
… _split cuts on whitespace alone, so s' and $'s stay glued to their words …
… and the parser walks down the ladder, one function per level, building nodes as it goes.
$'s binds last, so ceil applies to the whole quotient: ⌈job-size ÷ page-size⌉.
A parse error skips to end-<name>, so one run reports every broken function.
